content.title: About
content.content: Hot pickled peppers are fresh peppers that have been fermented in a vinegar brine with salt, spices, and sometimes sugar. They deliver a bright, fiery flavor, aromatic spice notes, and a crisp texture. Peppers are commonly enjoyed as a snack, a topping for dishes, or an ingredient in salads and sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickling preserves most of the vitamin C and A content, making them more nutritious than many other snack foods.
The heat comes from capsaicin, which also has a thermogenic effect.
Pickled peppers are a tradition in Mediterranean, Asian, and Latin American cuisines.
In some cultures, pickled peppers symbolize hospitality and celebration.
Peppers can range from tiny chilies to large sweet bell peppers, each with its own level of spiciness.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Capsaicin and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Boosts metabolism
items.content: Capsaicin may increase metabolic rate and help burn calories.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The acidic brine stimulates stomach acid production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy bowel function and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot peppers can irritate the stomach and esophageal lining, especially in people with gastritis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Pickled foods are often high in salt; individuals with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peppers or the spices in the brine.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity can cause heartburn in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peppers can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, sandwiches, pizza, pasta, or used in sauces. They also pair well with cheeses, charcuterie, and olives.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pickled peppers refrigerated in their original glass jar, tightly sealed. Properly stored, they retain flavor and quality for 3–4 months. Discard any that show mold, off‑odors, or discoloration.
